summary.text: Coastal flooding happens when seawater covers dry, low-lying land.
Seawater can flood straight in, wash over a barrier or break through one, and how far inland it reaches depends on the shape of the land.
Rising seas, more extreme weather and growing coastal populations have made the damage from these floods worse and affected more people.

facts.label: People in coastal zone
facts.value: Over 50 percent of the world's population

facts.label: Coastal zone defined
facts.value: Within 100 km of the coast and 100 m elevation

facts.label: Rare extremes now
facts.value: About four times more likely since 1900

facts.label: Classic example
facts.value: North Sea flood of 1953, Netherlands and eastern England

items.prompt: A seaside town pumps large amounts of water from wells near the shore for many years. How can this raise its flood risk?

options.label: The ground can sink lower over time
The nearby sea becomes much saltier
The local tides grow stronger
The offshore waves become taller

items.explain: Taking water out of coastal groundwater reservoirs can make the land subside, leaving it lower and easier to flood.

items.prompt: A town builds a sea wall to protect its main beach. What can this do to the stretch of coast next door?

options.label: Shield it from waves as well
Make it erode, raising its flood risk
Leave it completely unaffected
Build it up with extra sand

items.explain: Sea walls change the beach's natural processes, which can erode neighbouring coast and increase its flood risk.

items.prompt: During a storm, a strong wind blows from the sea toward the land for hours. What does this do to the water at the shore?

options.label: It lowers it by flattening the waves
It leaves the level unchanged
It piles the water up higher
It only raises water far offshore

items.explain: Onshore wind pushes water up against the coast, an effect called wind setup.

items.prompt: A deep low-pressure storm system sits over the ocean. What does the drop in air pressure do to the sea surface beneath it?

options.label: It sinks, because the air is lighter
It freezes into a thin crust
It stays flat, since air has no effect
It tends to rise higher

items.explain: Low atmospheric pressure in storms tends to raise the sea surface, which is called barometric setup.

items.prompt: Human-caused sea-level rise has changed how often historically rare extreme sea levels hit coasts. Since 1900, about how much more likely have they become?

options.label: About 10 percent more likely
About twice as likely
About four times as likely
About a hundred times as likely

items.explain: A 2026 study found these extreme coastal sea levels are roughly four times more likely than in 1900.

items.prompt: A coastal village wants to cut storm-wave damage without pouring concrete. Which step helps most?

options.label: Clearing shore plants so water drains
Keeping the mangrove forest on the shore
Draining wetlands to firm up the ground
Flattening dunes to widen the beach

items.explain: Mangroves and wetlands soak up wave energy and protect against storm waves, so natural defenses like these should be kept and protected.
